data.name: forklift
data.description: Forklift — a version control system designed for serverless hosting.

commands.title: Verify the warehouse's signed history offline
commands.description:
Verify the warehouse's signed history offline: the office chain back to the genesis parcel, then the given pallet (the current one by default). Requires established trust ("forklift office enroll").

By default, large chunked files are presence-checked (their chunks are confirmed present without re-reading the bytes). "--full" re-reads every present chunk — re-hashing it — and re-assembles each chunked file to confirm its recorded content hash; a stronger, slower pass.

full.description: Re-read and re-hash every present chunk, and re-assemble each chunked file to verify its content hash (a normal audit only presence-checks chunks)

pallet.description: The pallet to audit (default: the current pallet)

commands.title: Manage bays: parallel working directories bound to this warehouse
commands.description: Manage bays: additional working directories bound to this warehouse. A bay shares the object store, the refs and trust, but keeps its own working tree, inventory, current pallet and lock — so several agents (or you and an agent) work one machine without cloning the objects N times or fighting one lock. Like git worktrees, designed in. Without a subcommand, the bays are listed.

commands.title: Open a new bay (a new working directory on a new pallet)
commands.description: Open a bay: a new working directory bound to this warehouse, checked out to a new pallet named after the bay (branched from the current head). The bay shares this warehouse's objects, refs and trust; it has its own working tree, inventory and current pallet. cd into it to work there. A scoped bay (--scope) is how an orchestrator hands a sub-agent a task-scoped sandbox.

scope.description: Limit the bay to one or more subtree paths — a scoped (sparse) bay. Repeatable

name.description: The bay's name (also the name of the new pallet it checks out)

path.description: Where to create the working directory (default: a sibling of the warehouse)

commands.title: De-register a bay (its pallet ref and materialized files are kept)
commands.description: De-register a bay: remove its local state and the redirect in its working directory. The bay's pallet is a normal ref and is kept, and its materialized files are left in place — delete the directory yourself to reclaim the space.

commands.title: Show, for each line of a file, the parcel and author that last changed it
commands.description: Attribute every line of a file to the parcel that introduced it — and, because authorship is signed and classed, to the author's identity class and supervisor. That is blame git cannot express: "was this line written by a human or an agent, under whose supervision", offline and forge-proof. The walk follows the first-parent chain from the revision (the current pallet's head by default); a line a merge brought in from a side line is attributed to the merge parcel.

rev.description: The revision to blame at: a pallet name or a parcel hash (default: the current pallet's head)

commands.title: Clone a remote warehouse into a new directory
commands.description: Clone a remote warehouse: prepare a fresh warehouse in the target directory, remember the remote, adopt its trust anchor, download the history (using the remote's bundle when it has one) and materialize the chosen pallet in the working directory. With --only, clone sparsely: fetch the full signed history but only the named subtree(s) of content, leaving the rest sealed by hash. With --cache, mark the warehouse as a cache, which may lack content its history reaches.

pallet.description: The pallet to check out (default: the remote's default pallet)

token.description: The bearer token, when the remote requires one (remembered as "remote.token")

only.description: Clone sparsely: fetch only the named subtree path(s) of content. Repeatable

cache.description: Clone as a cache: a warehouse that may lack content its history reaches

expect.description: Refuse unless the remote's trust anchor is this genesis (an out-of-band pin)

url.description: The URL of the remote warehouse (e.g. http://forklift.example.com:9418)

directory.description: The directory to create the warehouse in (must be new or empty)

commands.title: Read or change configuration values
commands.description: Read or change configuration values (e.g. "remote.url"): list every known key, get one, set one or unset one. Values are stored in the current warehouse by default, and each subcommand's --global targets the per-user configuration that applies to all warehouses; when reading, the warehouse value wins over the global one. Without a subcommand, every known key is listed with its effective value.

commands.title: List every known key and its value (the default)

global.description: List the per-user configuration that applies to all warehouses

commands.title: Print the value of a key

global.description: Read the per-user configuration that applies to all warehouses

commands.title: Set a key to a value

global.description: Write the per-user configuration that applies to all warehouses

value.description: The value to set the key to

commands.title: Remove a key (e.g. clearing a "remote.token")

global.description: Remove the key from the per-user configuration that applies to all warehouses

commands.title: List the files left in conflict by an unresolved consolidation
commands.description: List the files an unresolved consolidation left in conflict, as structured records (with --json: each file's base, ours and theirs sides as content addresses a resolver can fetch). Designed for agents, which resolve merges well when given the three sides instead of marker soup. An empty list is a valid answer — there is nothing to resolve.

commands.title: Consolidate (merge) another pallet into the current one
commands.description: Consolidate (merge) another pallet into the current one. Fast-forwards when possible; otherwise runs a three-way merge and stacks a merge parcel. Conflicts are marked in the affected files and must be resolved, loaded and stacked to complete the consolidation.

pallet.description: The pallet whose head to merge into the current pallet

commands.title: Squash the current draft pallet onto a target as one clean parcel, keeping the trail
commands.description: Deliver the current (draft) pallet's checkpoint trail onto a target pallet as a single clean signed parcel — the squash agents need, without losing the trail. The delivered parcel carries the draft head's tree with the target as its only parent, so the checkpoints stay out of the target's history; the full trail is kept (the draft pallet is left intact) and recorded as a signed "delivery" entry on the parcel's manifest, so "what the agent tried, in what order" stays discoverable. Needs an enrolled key (the trail is signed evidence). The current pallet becomes the target; the working directory is unchanged (the tree is identical).

commands.title: Show line-by-line changes
commands.description: Show the line-by-line changes between the working directory and the inventory (what "forklift load" would stage). With --staged, show the changes between the inventory and the pallet head (what "forklift stack" would record). With two revisions (pallet names or parcel hashes), compare those instead — use ":empty" as either revision to compare against the empty tree (every file on the other side then lists as added). An optional trailing path limits the report to a file or directory.

staged.description: Compare the inventory against the pallet head (what "forklift stack" would record)

commands.title: Import a git repository's history into this warehouse (one-way migration)
commands.description: One-way migration of a git repository's history into this warehouse: git commits become parcels, trees become trees, blobs become blobs, and each local branch becomes a pallet. The imported history is unsigned (it predates trust), so import into a fresh warehouse and then run "forklift office enroll" to anchor it. Run it from the git repo's directory ("forklift git import .") so the checked-out working tree already holds the imported HEAD. Forklift converts nothing on checkout, so a file git converted (line endings, ident, a filter) reads as modified, and the import warns about it. Requires git on PATH.

no-compact.description: Store the imported objects loose instead of packing (and delta-compressing) them on the way in

path.description: The git repository to import from (e.g. \".\")

commands.title: Export this warehouse's history into a new git repository (one-way, lossy)
commands.description: One-way export of this warehouse's history into a new git repository: parcels become commits, trees become trees, blobs become blobs, and each user pallet becomes a branch. The escape hatch that makes trying forklift reversible — but lossy in this direction: git has no home for the signed office, the @manifest, or per-parcel signatures, so those are dropped. The path must be empty or new. Requires git on PATH.

path.description: Where to create the git repository (must be empty or new)

commands.title: Mirror the remote's pallets to a git remote (mirror.url), never by force
commands.description: Keep the git remote at mirror.url in step with the pallets the Forklift remote holds (mirror.pallets, or every user pallet). Each pallet's remote head is fetched, exported incrementally into .forklift/mirror.git, and pushed to the git branch of the same name, never by force: a git branch holding a commit the export does not is refused, and left as it is. Only lifted heads are mirrored. Tags, the signed office, the @manifest and signatures are not mirrored. A head is exported only once its history verifies against the trust anchor (the one held, or the one the remote serves). With mirror.auto on (the default), every lift mirrors the pallet it lifted. Requires git on PATH.

commands.title: Reviewable merge proposals (pull requests) on the @haul meta pallet
commands.description: Propose merging one pallet into another, with discussion and signed reviews — pull requests, in Forklift's vocabulary. A haul is a set of signed cells on the @haul meta pallet — its proposal, its proposed head, its status, one review per reviewer and its comments — so authorship, and who approved, is forge-proof and carries the operator's identity class (a human's approval is distinguishable from an agent's). A review names the head it reviewed, and a merged haul stays merged. Reviews are recorded; merging is not gated on them in this release. Intra-warehouse (pallet → pallet).

commands.title: Open a merge proposal

source.description: The pallet to merge from (default: the current pallet)

title.description: A short title for the proposal

commands.title: List proposals

state.description: Which to show: open (default) | merged | closed | all

commands.title: Show one proposal in full

id.description: The haul id (or a unique prefix)

commands.title: Propose the source pallet's current head
commands.description: Move an open haul to the source pallet's current head. Only the haul's opener moves it; a rewound or rebased source moves the haul with it. Reviews record the head they reviewed, so a review of an earlier head stays listed but no longer counts as an approval of the haul.

id.description: The haul id (or a unique prefix)

commands.title: Add a comment

id.description: The haul id (or a unique prefix)

commands.title: Land a proposal: consolidate its source into the target

id.description: The haul id (or a unique prefix)

commands.title: Close a proposal without merging

id.description: The haul id (or a unique prefix)

commands.title: Reopen a closed proposal

id.description: The haul id (or a unique prefix)

commands.title: Resolve a standing durability taint, or finish or undo an interrupted operation
commands.description:
Resolve a standing durability taint ("durability_taint" refusals, exit 21): a write's final path(s) were left visible after a failed durability sync, and the automatic entry-heal every command runs could not restage every one of them on its own. This verb runs the deeper recovery pass — restage whatever it can, then walk every durable ref source (pallet heads, parked work, and staged inventory shards) to tell a vanished-but-never-referenced object (safe to drop) from one something still points at (reported, with remedies). A torn taint (its own record was cut short by a crash) is resolved by rescanning the whole store, which takes longer. Exits 0 once every recorded path is resolved; exits 21, with the taint left standing on exactly what remains, otherwise.

It then finishes or undoes an operation that rewrites the whole staging area (shift, park, a merge, pick or fast-forward, lower, git import, bay creation) and was interrupted ("incomplete_load" refusals naming it, exit 20): rolled forward where the bay's state shows it got far enough, rolled back otherwise. Either way it rewrites only files that still hold one side's content or are missing; any other file (an edit made since, or a merge's combination of both sides) is left and reported as a local change, never staged.

commands.title: Print the parcels of a revision, newest first
commands.description: Print the parcels of the current pallet (or of the given revision — a pallet name or a parcel hash), newest first: hash, operators, timestamps and description. Read a long history in pages: --limit caps a page, and --after resumes from the cursor the previous page returned. To filter on identity, signer or provenance, use "forklift query".

limit.description: Show at most this many parcels (newest first) — a bounded walk that never loads the whole history

after.description: Resume paging from a cursor returned as `next` by a previous `--json` page (an opaque list of frontier parcels). Use with `-n` to read history in batches

oneline.description: One line per parcel: the abbreviated hash and the description's first line only (git's `log --oneline`). Skips the author, timestamps and full message — and the office/display-name work behind them — so it is the fastest way to scan history

revision.description: A pallet name or a parcel hash prefix (default: the current pallet)

commands.title: Upload the current pallet's new parcels to the remote (push)
commands.description: Upload the current pallet's new parcels to the configured remote ("remote.url") and move the remote's ref. When trust is established, the office pallet and the trust anchor are lifted first — the remote verifies every signature before it accepts the update. A remote that is ahead or has diverged is never overwritten: lower first when it is ahead; when both sides moved and the changes do not auto-merge, the refusal names how to merge the remote head in. A pallet deleted on the remote is re-created only with "--recreate", from work that descends from the head it was deleted at.

recreate.description: Re-create the pallet on the remote where it was deleted, acknowledging the deletion: refused unless the local work descends from the head the remote's tombstone holds

commands.title: Take the current state of a file or directory into the inventory (stage)

path.description: The file or directory to load

commands.title: Download the remote's new parcels and fast-forward the current pallet, or another (pull)
commands.description: Download the remote's new parcels for the current pallet from the configured remote ("remote.url") and fast-forward to them — working directory and inventory included. Naming another pallet downloads the remote's history of that pallet and creates or fast-forwards its ref alone: this bay, its files and its inventory stay where they are, and "forklift shift" moves onto it. On first contact with a trusted remote its trust anchor is adopted (one-way, like "forklift office enroll"), and the adopted genesis is reported. A diverged pallet is reported, never merged implicitly. A diverged metadata pallet (@kv, @tags, @manifest, @haul) replays the local changes onto the remote's; paths both sides changed refuse the lower with a meta_conflict error (exit 24) naming every pallet, path and both sides, until --keep resolves each one.

expect.description: Refuse unless the remote's trust anchor is this genesis (an out-of-band pin)

keep.description: Resolve a metadata conflict: keep ours or theirs at a path (repeatable)

confirm.description: Drop the local changes a "theirs" resolution names (only a "theirs" --keep needs it)

pallet.description: The pallet to lower (default: the current pallet); "forklift pallet list --remote" lists the remote's

commands.title: Facts recorded about a parcel after the fact: notes, approvals, provenance, keyed values
commands.description: Record and read the manifest — signed facts attached to a parcel after the fact. Notes, approvals and machine-authorship provenance are entries on the "@manifest" meta pallet (subcommands note, approve, provenance and show). Keyed values, such as a build status or a ticket link, live on the "@kv" meta pallet (subcommands set, get, unset, keys and log): a key holds one text value per parcel, and lower combines changes to different keys, while a key changed differently on both sides is a conflict that "forklift lower --keep" resolves. Every change is signed by its writer, verifiable offline against the office chain, and references the parcel without ever changing it. Recording needs an enrolled signing key; a keyed value also needs a writer or admin role. Without a subcommand, every "@manifest" entry is listed.

commands.title: Attach a free-form note to a parcel
commands.description: Record a signed note about a parcel — a review comment, a caveat, any free-form annotation. The note references the parcel and never changes it. Requires an enrolled signing key.

revision.description: The parcel the note is about (a pallet name, or a parcel hash / unique prefix)

commands.title: Record a signed approval (sign-off) of a parcel
commands.description: Record a signed approval of a parcel — a cryptographic sign-off, forge-proof and offline-verifiable. Optionally attach a message. Requires an enrolled signing key.

message.description: An optional message to attach to the approval

revision.description: The parcel to approve (a pallet name, or a parcel hash / unique prefix)

commands.title: Record how a parcel was produced: model, tool, session (AI provenance)
commands.description: Record signed machine-authorship provenance for a parcel — which model produced the change, with which tool, in which session, and (optionally) a transcript fingerprint. Because the entry is signed, it is evidence: paired with an agent-class identity ("forklift office admit --agent --supervisor"), it answers "which model produced this, under whose supervision" forge-proof and offline — the AI-traceability question git cannot answer. Requires an enrolled signing key.

model.description: The model that produced the change (e.g. claude-opus-4-8)

tool.description: The tool or agent that ran the model (e.g. claude-code)

session.description: The session / conversation id the change came from

transcript.description: A hash or fingerprint of the prompt / transcript

revision.description: The parcel the provenance is about (a pallet name, or a parcel hash / prefix)

commands.title: Show the manifest entries attached to a parcel
commands.description: Show every manifest entry (approvals, notes) attached to a parcel, oldest first, with who recorded each and when.

revision.description: The parcel whose manifest to show (a pallet name, or a parcel hash / prefix)

commands.title: Set a keyed value on a parcel
commands.description: Set a key on a parcel to a text value, replacing any value it held. A key is ASCII letters, digits, ".", "_" and "-", at most 128 bytes, and never begins with "." or "-"; a value is at most 64 KiB of text. Requires an enrolled signing key and a writer or admin role.

revision.description: The parcel the value is about (a pallet name, or a parcel hash / unique prefix)

commands.title: Show a keyed value on a parcel

revision.description: The parcel (a pallet name, or a parcel hash / unique prefix)

commands.title: Remove a keyed value from a parcel
commands.description: Remove a key from a parcel. A key that holds no value is refused. Requires an enrolled signing key and a writer or admin role.

revision.description: The parcel (a pallet name, or a parcel hash / unique prefix)

commands.title: List every keyed value, or a parcel's

revision.description: Only this parcel's values (a pallet name, or a parcel hash / unique prefix)

commands.title: Show every change to a key, newest first, with who made it
commands.description: Show every change to a key on a parcel, newest first: the parcel that made it, when, by whom, and the value after it. Walks the whole history of the @kv meta pallet.

revision.description: The parcel (a pallet name, or a parcel hash / unique prefix)

commands.title: Manage the warehouse office: users and signing keys
commands.description: Manage the warehouse office: users and signing keys, tracked as metadata on the "@office" meta pallet. Without a subcommand, the users and their keys are listed.

commands.title: Enroll the configured operator and establish trust — one-way!
commands.description: Enroll the configured operator and establish trust: the genesis office parcel introduces the first user and key. This is a one-way door — from then on every parcel stacked in this warehouse must be signed. When a remote is configured, its pallet heads are included in the trust boundary (history the remote already has stays valid unsigned), so the remote must be reachable — or pass --offline to skip it.

offline.description: Skip the configured remote (its heads will not be in the trust boundary)

passphrase.description: Protect the new key with a passphrase (recommended for human operators)

commands.title: Enroll another operator with their public key — admins only
commands.description: Enroll another operator: their UUID, public key and proof-of-possession, exactly as printed by their "forklift profile keygen" run. The key becomes their identity root, endorsed by your admin key. Office records are pseudonymous — no names or emails ever go on-chain. Mark automated principals with --agent / --bot / --service: the class rides in the signed record, so "an agent wrote this, supervised by <human>" is forge-proof. An agent requires a --supervisor; a supervisor must be an enrolled human. Automated identities should hold passphraseless keys (they sign autonomously under their own marked identity, never as a human).

role.description: The operator's role: admin, writer or reader

pallet.description: Restrict a writer to these pallets (repeatable; default: all pallets)

agent.description: Mark this operator as an AI agent (requires --supervisor)

bot.description: Mark this operator as an automation bot

service.description: Mark this operator as a service / CI identity

operator-id.description: The operator's UUID (printed by their "forklift profile keygen")

public-key.description: The operator's public key (64 hex characters)

pop.description: The key's proof-of-possession (printed by their "forklift profile keygen")

commands.title: Link another device's key to your own identity
commands.description: Link another device's key to your own identity: a sigchain endorsement — the new key is trusted because a key you already hold signs for it, so every warehouse that trusts your identity accepts it automatically. Run "forklift profile keygen" on the other device (configured with the same operator.uuid) and pass the printed public key and proof-of-possession here.

public-key.description: The new key's public half (64 hex characters)

pop.description: The new key's proof-of-possession (printed by "forklift profile keygen")

commands.title: Authorize a new key for an already-enrolled operator — admins only
commands.description: Authorize a new key for an already-enrolled operator: the recovery path for someone who lost every device (the scope of a key-authorization equals the scope of the authorizer's authority, so an admin's endorsement is valid exactly here, in the office they administer). The operator runs "forklift profile keygen" on their new machine and hands you the printed line over a channel where you can confirm it is really them; their proof-of-possession still co-signs the record, so you cannot attribute a key they do not hold. For your own devices use "forklift office link"; for a new operator use "forklift office admit".

operator-id.description: The enrolled operator's UUID (printed by their "forklift profile keygen")

public-key.description: The new key's public half (64 hex characters)

pop.description: The new key's proof-of-possession (printed by "forklift profile keygen")

commands.title: Change a user's role (and a writer's pallet grants) — admins only
commands.description: Change a user's role (admin, writer or reader) and, for writers, the pallet grants. Admins only, with lockout protection: the office always keeps at least one admin. Remotes enforce roles on every lift.

pallet.description: Restrict a writer to these pallets (repeatable; default: all pallets)

role.description: The new role: admin, writer or reader

commands.title: Issue a fresh key for the configured operator and retire the old ones
commands.description: Issue a fresh key for the configured operator and retire the old ones. The change is signed with the old key, proving the rotation was authorized by its owner. Each retirement records a distrust boundary (the pallet heads vouched for right now, the remote's included), so a retired key cannot silently sign anything new.

offline.description: Skip the configured remote (its heads will not join the distrust boundary)

passphrase.description: Protect the new key with a passphrase (recommended for human operators)

commands.title: Revoke a key: retire it, or mark it compromised
commands.description: Revoke a key. Plain retirement is the routine goodbye (a decommissioned machine); --compromised marks a key that may be in someone else's hands. Either way the revocation records a distrust boundary — the pallet heads vouched for right now, the remote's included: signatures by the key outside that ancestry fail every future audit. Exact ancestry, never timestamps, so a shifted clock cannot forge validity.

compromised.description: The key may be in someone else's hands (recorded as the revocation reason)

offline.description: Skip the configured remote (its heads will not join the distrust boundary)

key-id.description: The id of the key to revoke

commands.title: RESET trust: new root, prior history pinned as attested — recovery only
commands.description: Re-genesis: the recovery primitive for a chain nobody can extend anymore (all keys lost, no admin left). Creates a new self-endorsed trust root for the configured operator and replaces the trust anchor; the old office head is pinned in the new anchor as attested history (kept, but its guarantee degrades from verified to attested). LOUD: every clone refuses to sync until its holder consciously re-accepts, and a remote accepts the reset only from the server operator's static token. Without --confirm, prints what would happen.

confirm.description: Reset trust (without it, what the reset would do is shown and nothing changes)

commands.title: Consciously accept a remote's trust reset (re-genesis)
commands.description: Accept a remote's re-genesis: after a trust reset every sync is refused until you deliberately accept the new anchor — the SSH host-key-change moment. The new anchor must name your pinned genesis as its prior (the chain of custody); verify out-of-band that the reset is legitimate before confirming. Without --confirm, shows what would be accepted and refuses. --confirm takes the new genesis being accepted, and accepts only if that is still the remote's genesis — so what is accepted is exactly what was shown.

confirm.description: Accept the new anchor, whose genesis must be this value (without it, the reset is only described)

commands.title: List the users and their keys (the default)
Manage pallets (branches): list, create, delete and restore them
commands.description: Manage pallets, Forklift's branches. Without a subcommand, the pallets are listed, as "forklift pallet list" does.

commands.title: List the pallets, marking the current one (the default)
commands.description: List the pallets, marking the current one. With "--remote", list the remote's pallets instead, each with how it relates to the local one, and the pallets deleted there.

all.description: Also show the meta pallets (the office and other tracked metadata; reach them with the "@" qualifier, e.g. "forklift history @office")

remote.description: List the remote's pallets instead: each with its remote head, the local head, and whether the two are the same, the local one is ahead, or they differ (lower decides), and the pallets deleted there. Downloads and writes nothing

commands.title: Create a new pallet and shift to it
commands.description: Create a new pallet at the current head, or at the given revision (a pallet name or a parcel hash), and shift to it.

name.description: The name of the new pallet

revision.description: Where the new pallet starts: a pallet name or a parcel hash prefix (default: the current pallet's head)

commands.title: Delete a pallet: remove its ref, keeping its parcels
commands.description: Delete a pallet: its ref goes, its parcels stay, and "forklift undo" brings it back. Refused for the pallet a bay stands on, one an open haul names, and, without "--force", one whose work no other pallet here or on the remote holds. With "--remote", delete the remote's pallet instead: it keeps its history on the remote, and no clone's own pallet changes.

force.description: Delete even when no other pallet holds the pallet's work. It stays recoverable by "forklift undo" while the delete is in this bay's undo journal, and in a warehouse a server has served by "forklift pallet restore" while its tombstone stands

remote.description: Delete the remote's pallet instead of the local one

commands.title: Bring back a deleted pallet at the head its tombstone holds
commands.description: Bring back a pallet deleted in this warehouse after it was served, at the head its tombstone holds. Refused while a bay stands on the name at another head. With "--remote", bring it back on the remote, which needs no history here.

remote.description: Bring the remote's pallet back instead of the local one

commands.title: Park the work in progress and reset to the pallet head
commands.description: Park the work in progress (the staged and unstaged changes of tracked files) as a parked parcel and reset the warehouse to the pallet head. Untracked files are left alone. "forklift park pop" re-applies the latest parked changes; "forklift park list" lists them.

commands.title: Re-apply the most recently parked changes (staged) and drop them from the list
List the parked parcels, newest first
Apply a parcel's changes onto the current pallet as a new, author-preserving parcel
commands.description: Apply a parcel's diff (its change against its first parent) onto the current pallet as a new, author-preserving, freshly-signed parcel. Unlike rebase, pick only *adds* — no rewrite, no force-push: the picked parcel's authors are preserved and this operator is recorded as the stacker. A clean pick is stacked immediately; a conflicting one leaves markers to resolve, "forklift load" and "forklift stack" (which completes the pick single-parent).

message.description: The new parcel's message (default: the source parcel's message)

revision.description: The parcel to pick: a pallet name, or a parcel hash / unique prefix

commands.title: Prepare a new warehouse in the current directory
commands.description: Prepare a new warehouse in the current directory: the ".forklift" folder with the object store, the staging area and the configuration template. No ignore file is written: ".forkliftignore" is tracked content, created when you need one. Preparing is idempotent — only the missing pieces are created.

commands.title: Manage identity profiles (named operator ids) and select one per warehouse
commands.description: Manage identity profiles: named operator ids stored in the global configuration. A warehouse selects one with "forklift profile use", so one machine can act as different operators in different warehouses — e.g. a personal identity and one per organization. "forklift profile keygen" generates a signing key for one. Without a subcommand, the profiles are listed.

commands.title: List the profiles and the local keys each one holds (the default)
Create a named profile (mints an operator id unless one is given)

id.description: The operator id (e.g. one issued by a hosting provider); minted when omitted

commands.title: Act as this profile in the current warehouse
Generate a keypair locally and print its public half + proof-of-possession
commands.description: Generate a keypair locally and print its public half plus a proof-of-possession (a self-signature binding the key to an operator id). The private key stays on this machine. Hand the printed admit line to an office admin to be enrolled, or the printed link line to a machine that already holds one of your keys to add this as another device. With a profile name, the key belongs to that profile's operator id. Without one, it belongs to the identity this directory acts as: the profile the enclosing warehouse selects, else the globally selected profile, else the warehouse's operator.identifier, else the global one (the default identity). It says which one it used. Runs outside a warehouse too, and records nothing in one.

passphrase.description: Protect the new key with a passphrase (recommended for human operators)

name.description: The profile whose operator id the key belongs to; omit it for the current identity

commands.title: Query parcel history by signed identity, signer and parcel facts
commands.description: Filter parcel history on its signed dimensions — identity class, supervisor, role, signing key, recorded machine-authorship provenance, signed tags — plus parcel-local facts (dates, description, merge-ness, touched paths). By default identity answers are VERIFIED: the signature is checked and the office joined off the verified signer, never off the parcel's own (forgeable) claim; --recorded opts into the cheap, self-declared reading and labels every answer accordingly. A parcel with no provenance recorded at all never matches a --model/--tool predicate in either direction (absence isn't a claim to negate); an untagged parcel plainly does not carry a --tag. Flags AND together; --where takes a JSON predicate tree for or/not/nesting. Scope the walk with revisions and --from — that (not --limit) is what bounds verification work. A match signed by a since-revoked key carries signer.boundary: vouched (inside the history its revocation vouched for), suspect (outside it: a forged backdate, or the key's holder kept signing after the revocation), or unresolved (a partial clone lacks a boundary head or an ancestor of one, so the question cannot be answered here; never read it as suspect). A --where leaf on signer.boundary filters on vouched or suspect.

from.description: Exclude this revision and all its ancestors from the walk (git's A..B shape)

class.description: Verified author identity class: human | agent | bot | service

unsupervised.description: Verified author is automated (agent/bot/service) and has no supervisor

supervisor.description: Verified author is supervised by this operator id

author-after.description: Only parcels authored after this RFC 3339 timestamp

author-before.description: Only parcels authored before this RFC 3339 timestamp

merges.description: Only merge parcels (more than one parent)

grep.description: Description matches this glob (*, ?) or contains it as a substring

model.description: Recorded machine-authorship model matches this glob (*, ?) or contains it as a substring (from a manifest provenance entry; absence of any entry never matches)

tool.description: Recorded machine-authorship tool matches this glob (*, ?) or contains it as a substring (from a manifest provenance entry; absence of any entry never matches)

tag.description: Carries this signed tag (from the @tags meta pallet)

touches.description: Changed this warehouse path (or a path under it) versus the parcel's first parent only — a merge whose result at the path already matches its first parent (e.g. both sides added identical content) does not match, even if the other parent touched it (see "forklift help query")

verify.description: Verify identity answers (the default; the flag exists to say so explicitly)

recorded.description: Use the recorded (self-declared, forgeable) identity instead of verifying: cheaper, prunes early, and every answer is labeled "recorded"

where.description: A JSON predicate tree ("-" reads it from stdin) AND-ed with the flags

limit.description: Show at most this many matches (bounds the output page, never the verification work — scope the walk with revisions or --from for that)

after.description: Resume paging from a cursor returned as `next` by a previous `--json` page

oneline.description: One line per match: the abbreviated hash and the description's first line

revisions.description: Walk from these revisions (pallet names or parcel hashes; default: the current pallet's head)

commands.title: Stage a file or directory for removal
commands.description: Stage a file or directory for removal: its inventory entries are marked as deleted, so they will not be part of the next parcel. The working directory is not touched. To unstage changes instead (undo a "forklift load"), use "forklift unload".

path.description: The file or directory to stage for removal

commands.title: Restore a file or directory from the inventory (discard unstaged changes)
commands.description: Restore a file or directory in the working directory from the inventory (discard unstaged changes). When that would overwrite a changed file, it lists the files whose changes would be lost, changes nothing and exits non-zero unless --confirm is given; restoring a missing file needs no --confirm. To unstage instead, leaving the working directory untouched, use "forklift unload".

confirm.description: Discard the unstaged changes the restore would overwrite

path.description: The file or directory to restore

commands.title: Manage the `fl` short alias for this binary
commands.description: Manage the `fl` short alias: a shell-agnostic symlink (a shim on Windows) placed next to this binary, not a per-shell alias — it works in scripts, non-interactive shells and every shell dialect alike, and is trivially discoverable and removable. This is the one implementation every install method (the curl script, pult, `cargo install`) calls, so the alias never drifts between install paths. Without a subcommand, reports whether the alias is installed and where.

commands.title: Create the alias next to this binary (default name: "fl")
commands.description: Create the alias next to this binary: on Unix, a symlink; on Windows (where a symlink needs elevated privilege), a `.cmd` shim that forwards to this binary. Resolves this binary's own path (`current_exe`), so it always points at whichever `forklift` is actually running the command. Idempotent: an alias that already points here succeeds without change. Refuses — without a --force, there isn't one — if the name is already taken by something else (a real file, or a symlink to a different target): removing an unrelated file automatically would be a surprise no flag should paper over.

commands.title: Remove the alias next to this binary (default name: "fl")
commands.description: Remove the alias next to this binary. A no-op (success) if it is not installed. Refuses if the name exists but was not created by this command (a real file, e.g.). A symlink (Unix) or a recognized shim (Windows) is removed even if it points at a different forklift binary — deleting a symlink can never lose data, unlike a real file.

commands.title: Report whether the alias is installed and where it points (the default)
Check for a newer release and update this binary (client only)
commands.description: Check the latest published release against this binary and, for a script/manual install, update in place by re-running the verified install script. A package-manager install (cargo/brew) is never overwritten — self update shows the right upgrade command instead. There is deliberately no server self update: a server is redeployed, not self-mutated.

check.description: Only report whether an update is available and how to get it; change nothing

commands.title: Shift to another pallet
commands.description: Shift to another pallet: materialize its head parcel in the working directory and repopulate the inventory from it. Refuses to run while there are staged or unstaged changes (untracked files are tolerated). Shifting to the current pallet catches up with it when another bay or process moved it: a clean bay's files move to its head.

commands.title: Print a file's content at a revision, as git show does for REV:PATH
commands.description: Print a file's content at a revision in one invocation: "<revision>:<path>", split on the first ":" (a revision — a pallet name, an "@"-qualified meta pallet, or a parcel hash prefix — can never contain ":", so the split is unambiguous even when the path itself has one). A chunked large file reports its metadata (content hash, size, chunk count) instead of assembling it; non-text content is reported binary. With --json, the envelope carries the resolved parcel hash, the tree entry's own hash, the binary/chunked signal, and the content when it is text.

commands.title: Stack the inventory as a new parcel (commit) on the current pallet
commands.description: Stack the inventory as a new parcel (commit) on the current pallet, with the configured operator recorded as the author. A consolidation in progress is completed by this command.

commands.title: Report the staged and unstaged changes of the warehouse
commands.description: Report the current pallet, the staged changes (inventory vs pallet head — what the next "forklift stack" records) and the changes not yet loaded (working directory vs inventory). With --summary, report only the counts (a token-cheap overview for scripts and agents).

summary.description: Report only the counts, not the per-path changes

commands.title: Show and change the sparse scopes: this checkout's scope and the warehouse fetch scope
commands.description: Show and change the two sparse scopes. The checkout scope is what one checkout (a bay or the main tree) writes to disk; the fetch scope is what the warehouse's store holds, shared by every checkout. Without a subcommand, show both, as "forklift scope status" does. "forklift scope narrow" shrinks the checkout scope; "forklift scope fetch" widens the fetch scope and "forklift scope prune" shrinks it.

commands.title: Show this checkout's scope and the warehouse fetch scope (the default)
commands.description: Show the two sparse scopes: this checkout's scope (the subtree path(s) the bay or the main tree checks out, stages and stacks) and the warehouse's fetch scope (what the store has fetched at all). An unscoped bay (or the main tree) reports a full checkout scope: the whole tree. A checkout scope is local to the checkout and never tracked. Read-only.

commands.title: Widen a sparse warehouse's fetch scope and download the newly in-scope subtree(s)
commands.description: Widen a sparse warehouse's fetch scope: add subtree path(s) to what the store fetches, then download their content across the whole history from the remote. Cheap and incremental — only the newly in-scope objects are fetched; what is already present is skipped. Every checkout's scope stays as it is: after fetching, a bay can be scoped to the new path ("forklift bay add --scope"). A full (non-sparse) warehouse already holds everything, so there is nothing to fetch.

paths.description: The subtree path(s) to add to the fetch scope. Repeatable

commands.title: Narrow this checkout's scope and remove the dropped subtree(s) from the working directory
commands.description: Narrow this checkout's scope: drop subtree path(s) from what this bay (or the main tree) checks out, and remove the now out-of-scope files from the working directory. This frees nothing in the shared object store — the dropped content is still ordinary reachable history, not garbage — it only shrinks what this checkout shows, and the fetch scope stays as it is. A checkout must keep at least one in-scope path; to stop scoping entirely, open a fresh full checkout.

paths.description: The in-scope subtree path(s) to drop. Repeatable

commands.title: Reclaim disk from a sparse warehouse: shrink its fetch scope and free the content
commands.description: Reclaim disk from a sparse warehouse: drop a fetched path from the shared warehouse fetch scope and free the objects under it from the object store. This is the deliberate, destructive counterpart of "forklift scope narrow": narrow shrinks one checkout's scope and frees nothing, because narrowed-away content is still reachable history that garbage collection correctly keeps; prune shrinks the fetch scope warehouse-wide and reclaims its disk. It is multi-bay-aware: it refuses to free a path any checkout (the main tree or a bay) still has in its scope. It frees only history the remote holds, so it asks the remote first and refuses, changing nothing, when it cannot; work never lifted keeps its content until it is lifted and the prune is run again. What it frees is sealed by hash afterwards — fetched again from the origin with "forklift scope fetch". A full (non-sparse) warehouse has nothing to prune. If an earlier prune was interrupted before it finished freeing everything, running it again on the same path resumes and finishes the job rather than refusing. Without --confirm it shows what it would free, changes nothing and exits non-zero; when there is nothing to free, it runs without --confirm. A confirmed run plans again, so if the remote moved meanwhile it may free a little more or less than the preview showed.

confirm.description: Free the content (without it, what would be freed is shown and nothing changes)

paths.description: The fetched path(s) to prune. Repeatable; also accepts a path an earlier, interrupted prune already dropped from the fetch scope, to resume and finish freeing it

commands.title: Show the remote and the origin, or move a partial warehouse's origin to another server
commands.description: Show where this warehouse lifts to and lowers from: the configured remote ("remote.url") and, in a partial warehouse (one cloned with "--only" or "--cache"), its origin, with any move of the origin that has not finished. A partial warehouse talks only to its origin, the remote it was cloned from, because only the origin was proved to hold the content it lacks; "forklift remote move" is the one way to change it. A full warehouse has no origin and may talk to any remote.

commands.title: Move a partial warehouse's origin to another server that holds its content
commands.description: Point a partial warehouse at a new origin. The move first records that it is under way, so nothing fetches, lifts or changes what it checks until it ends. It then asks the new server for its pallets, judges its trust anchor as "forklift lower" would, fetches the parcels and signatures it lacks (no content), and checks that the new server holds everything this warehouse leans on its origin for: every tree, file and chunk that something here references and this warehouse does not hold. Only then does it rewrite the origin and "remote.url" (and "remote.token" with --token). If the check fails, nothing is rewritten and the origin stays; when the new server lacks content, copy the old server's warehouse to it server-side and run the move again. A move that stopped before it started rewriting can be abandoned with "forklift remote abort"; one that stopped while rewriting is finished by running the move again. A full warehouse has no origin: set "remote.url" with "forklift config set" instead.

token.description: The bearer token for the new origin, stored as remote.token when the move completes (default: the current remote.token)

commands.title: Abandon a move that stopped before it started rewriting the origin
commands.description: Abandon a move of the origin that stopped before it started rewriting: the origin and "remote.url" stay as they were, and fetching and lifting work again. A move that stopped while rewriting cannot be abandoned, because part of this warehouse already points at the new server; run the move again to finish it. With no move under way, it reports that and changes nothing.

commands.title: Inspect and maintain the object store: its health, packing, raw records and cached content
commands.description: Inspect and maintain the object store. Without a subcommand, report its health, as "forklift store status" does.

commands.title: Report object-store health: loose vs packed objects, packs, and whether compaction is due (the default)
commands.description: Report the health of the object store — the counterpart of "forklift stocktake" (which reports the working tree). Shows how many objects are loose (unpacked) versus packed, how many pack files there are and how delta-dense they are, the on-disk sizes, and whether an incremental compaction or a consolidating repack is currently due per the maintenance.loose / maintenance.packs thresholds. Read-only; run "forklift store compact" to act on it.

commands.title: Compact the object store: pack loose objects into a few dense pack files
commands.description: Compact the object store: sweep the loose objects (each its own zstd-compressed file) into a few dense pack files — an append-only data file plus a sorted index. At scale that turns hundreds of thousands of tiny files into a handful of large ones, so a history walk stops paying an open-per-object and the store stops paying per-file slack. Objects are only moved, never re-hashed; a loose file is deleted only after the pack that holds it is durably written, so compacting can never lose an object. Packs roll over at a size/count threshold, so no single pack grows unbounded. Run it after a large "forklift git import" or periodically as maintenance. With --all, also rewrite the existing packs: drop unreachable (garbage) objects that were stuck in packs and consolidate many packs into few — a heavier full repack, worth running occasionally. Add --redelta to a full repack to also re-delta-compress every object instead of copying already-packed records verbatim — denser, but a one-shot CPU-bound pass.

all.description: Repack existing packs too: drop unreachable objects and consolidate (a full repack)

redelta.description: Re-encode every object to delta-compress across the whole store (only with --all)

commands.title: Peek into an object (print its content)
commands.description: Print the content of an object: a blob's bytes, a tree's entries, or a parcel's fields. With --inventory, print the inventory of a working-directory folder instead.

inventory.description: Peek into the inventory of a working-directory folder instead of an object

object.description: The hash of the object to peek into

commands.title: Free cached content the origin holds, to be fetched again when read
commands.description: Free disk in a cache warehouse (one cloned with "--cache"): delete the content its origin holds and nothing here needs, so that a later read fetches it again. Parcels and signatures always stay. It asks the origin which history it holds first, and refuses, changing nothing, when the configured remote is not the origin or the origin cannot be reached; work never lifted keeps its content. It keeps every checkout's files, metadata and trust records, staged work, and anything a parked or in-progress operation needs. If it is interrupted, running it again finishes the job. Objects inside packs are not freed yet. Use --dry-run to see what it would free without changing anything.

dry-run.description: Report what would be freed and change nothing

commands.title: Manage signed tags: named, admin-signed pointers at a parcel (releases)
commands.description: Manage tags: named, signed pointers at a parcel — releases and milestones. A tag is a signed record on the "@tags" meta pallet, so who cut it is the parcel's signature (forge-proof), verifiable offline against the office chain. The release convention: a tag is signed by an admin key, so creating one requires an admin. Tag names are immutable. Without a subcommand, the tags are listed.

commands.title: Create a signed tag pointing at a revision (admin only)
commands.description: Create a signed tag pointing at a revision — a release marker. The tag is signed and recorded on the "@tags" meta pallet, verifiable offline against the office chain. As the release convention, only an admin may cut a tag. Tag names are immutable; an existing name is refused.

name.description: The tag name (a release label, e.g. "v1.2.0")

revision.description: The revision to tag: a pallet name or a parcel hash (default: the current pallet head)

commands.title: Show one tag in full (subject, tagger, message)
List every tag (the default)
Undo the last stack, consolidate, pick, shift or pallet delete
commands.description: Undo the last journaled operation: a "forklift stack", "forklift consolidate", "forklift pick", "forklift shift" or "forklift pallet delete". A stack, consolidate or pick is reversed softly: the pallet head moves back while the working directory and the inventory stay as they are (like git's "reset --soft HEAD~1"), so the undone changes are staged again and can be re-stacked — e.g. with a corrected message or author. A shift is reversed by shifting back. Undo reverses only the user's last operation: except for a pallet delete, which changed nothing in the bay, if the current pallet has been switched (e.g. by pallet create or deliver), its head has moved, or a consolidation or pick was started or finished since the journaled operation, it refuses instead of reaching past that. In a warehouse that has been served, a stack, consolidate or pick is not undone when it would move a user pallet back off the head it left, since the warehouse's clones may rely on that head: stack a parcel that reverts the change instead. An unreadable journal is reported by name, never read as empty. A pallet delete is reversed by bringing the pallet back at the head it was deleted at; if that name has been taken since, "--as <new-name>" brings it back under another name.

as.description: When the last journaled operation is a pallet delete: bring the deleted pallet back under this name instead of its own. The bay stays where it is

commands.title: Unstage a file or directory (keep your changes)
commands.description: Unstage a file or directory: reset its inventory entries to the pallet head, leaving the working directory untouched — the inverse of "forklift load". To stage a removal instead, use "forklift remove".

path.description: The file or directory to unstage

commands.title: Print the version of Forklift
